**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/22 (Mon) 14:22
- [USER] User inquired about the susceptibility to adverse reactions during a facial due to medications or medical conditions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Certain medications and medical conditions can make an individual more susceptible to adverse reactions during a facial.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Medications that thin blood, such as aspirin or Warfarin, may increase the risk of bruising or swelling after facial treatments.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Medical conditions like rosacea, eczema, or psoriasis may lead to increased skin irritation from certain facial ingredients or treatments.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Individuals should inform their esthetician about their medical history, medications, and known allergies or sensitivities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Precautions include using gentle or hypoallergenic products, avoiding aggressive exfoliation or extractions, and using cooling or anti-inflammatory ingredients.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Individuals may be advised to avoid certain treatments, such as chemical peels or microdermabrasion, until their medical condition or medication use has stabilized.
- [USER] User asked if they can still get a facial with a severe sunburn.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is not advisable to get a facial with a severe sunburn as it can aggravate the skin and cause pain or discomfort.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Sunburned skin is more sensitive and can easily become irritated by facial products and techniques.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The heat from steam and warm towels can cause more discomfort, and exfoliating or cleansing products may be too harsh.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is advisable to wait until the sunburn has completely healed before getting a facial.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended care for sunburn includes gentle treatment, staying hydrated, and using a good quality after-sun soothing lotion.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] If there is significant pain or blistering, consulting a healthcare professional is advised.
- [USER] User inquired about getting a facial with an active cold sore outbreak.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is best to avoid getting a facial with an active cold sore outbreak due to the contagious nature of the herpes simplex virus (HSV-1).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The esthetician's tools and products can cause minor trauma to the skin, exacerbating the cold sore outbreak.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Massage or pressure during a facial can be painful for those with a cold sore.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is best to wait until the cold sore has completely healed before getting a facial.
